title: Cursor vs Claude Code
summary: Cursor vs Claude Code: developers choosing an editor-centered or command-oriented repository workflow.

sections.heading: Keep the task identical
paragraphs: Use an existing failing test and the same repository snapshot. For Cursor, evaluate how comfortably you inspect changes in the editor. For Claude Code, evaluate the task and command loop. Both products have more than one surface; this comparison does not claim either is limited to one interface.

sections.heading: Permission boundaries
paragraphs: Before running commands, define which files and services are off limits. Reject a solution that requires weakening tests or sharing production secrets. A faster first response is not evidence of a safer change.

sections.heading: When neither is a fit
paragraphs: If your required security, data location or operating environment is not supported by current evidence, pause the purchase. Use the sources below to resolve the missing constraint before accepting a recommendation.

verdict: Choose the workflow you can inspect most reliably: editor-centered iteration or a terminal-oriented task loop. Neither choice removes code review.
bestFor: Developers choosing an editor-centered or command-oriented repository workflow
notFor: Teams needing a verified offline or data-residency guarantee
migration: Trial the candidate on a branch; retain the original workflow until tests, export and billing checks pass.
gaps: Verify the account's Privacy Mode and team setting, use of personal API keys, enabled non-ZDR model approvals, Cloud Agent use and applicable agreement before drawing account-specific processing or retention conclusions; no account settings were inspected.

pros.text: Cursor documents an editor and coding-agent workflow, with MCP support for local stdio and remote transports.
Claude Code documents terminal, IDE, desktop and web surfaces, so the choice is not limited to an editor versus a shell.

cons.text: Cursor requests approval before MCP tool calls by default; configured run modes can change handling for allowlisted tools.
Claude Code project MCP server configuration is not trusted until the workspace is trusted and its servers are approved.

faqs.question: Which MCP transports do their docs list?
faqs.answer: Cursor documents local stdio and local or remote SSE and Streamable HTTP; Claude Code documents local stdio and remote HTTP or WebSocket, with SSE deprecated.

faqs.question: Does terminal-oriented mean Claude Code has no editor option?
faqs.answer: No. Its docs list IDE, desktop and web surfaces as well as terminal use; test the surface available to your account.

faqs.question: Does Claude Code's self-hosted environment keep model inference on your infrastructure?
faqs.answer: No. Anthropic documents customer-operated runners for cloud-session compute, but inference still goes outbound to api.anthropic.com. The feature is a public beta for Team and Enterprise, is off by default, and does not establish an account's enabled state.

faqs.question: What does Cursor Privacy Mode cover, and what should an account verify?
faqs.answer: Cursor says Privacy Mode prevents training on Customer Data and that most model requests use provider zero-data-retention agreements, subject to safety and abuse review and non-ZDR model exceptions. Requests made with personal API keys still pass through Cursor's backend and rely on the provider's terms for retention. Optional Cloud Agents store encrypted repository copies while a run is active, then delete them after completion. Teams and Enterprise can enforce Privacy Mode; Cursor says individual plans follow its Privacy Policy rather than the commercial DPA. Verify the account setting, organization policy, model approvals, API-key route, Cloud Agent use and applicable agreement; none was inspected here.
